title: How many sheep and goats are there in all?
description: The world has about ten to the power nine sheep and about the same number of goats. Adding the two equal amounts doubles the number, so the power of ten stays the same. The other choices multiply or raise the power far too much.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding two equal amounts doubles the number and does not change the power of ten. Watch for students who add the bases or the exponents of the powers.

video_script.why: Two equal amounts added together make double, which is two times the same power of ten.
video_script.substitution: Add the two equal amounts as one billion and one billion, then write the total with one digit in front of the power of ten.
video_script.anchor: about 10⁹ sheep and about 10⁹ goats in the world
video_script.payoff_line: Adding two equal amounts doubles the number and keeps the power of ten

final_answer.spoken: The total is two times ten to the power nine. Ten to the power nine plus ten to the power nine is the same number.

video_script.design: The six choices from the book sit in a column at the right. The sum of the two equal amounts is built at the left, and each wrong choice is struck off in the working area.
